text: secundum Dei Patris providentiam electis, Spirituque lustratis, ut obediant, et Jesu Christi sanguine conspergantur, gratiam et pacem plurimam dicit.
note: *Deī Patris* capital, God the Father (θεοῦ πατρός, BSB "God the Father"; decision 20), as your *Deus et Pater*; *Spīritūque* capital, the Holy Spirit who sanctifies (ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, BSB "sanctified by the Spirit"), as your 1 Tim 3:16 *per Spīritum* (uncertain: Castellio's *spīritūque lūstrātīs* could be read of the believers' spirit; 1573 lower case) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Gratias agimus Deo, Patrique Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui nos pro sua singulari misericordia, Christum ex mortuis suscitando, regenuit in vividam spem,
note: *Patrīque* capital, God the Father of our Lord (ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου; decision 20), as your *Deō et Patrī* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: scrutantes, quodnam aut quale tempus indicaret Christi Spiritus, quo erant praediti, praesignificans et Christi supplicia, et deinde secuturam gloriam.
note: *Chrīstī Spīritus* capital, the Spirit of Christ in the prophets (τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ, BSB "the Spirit of Christ"; decision 20), as your Rom 8:9 *Chrīstī Spīritum* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quibus demonstratum est non ipsos sibi, sed vobis ea administrare, quae nunc vobis nuntiata sunt, per eos, qui vos in evangelio instituerunt, per Spiritum Sanctum de caelo missum, quae cupiunt ipsi angeli perspicere.
note: *Spīritum Sānctum* both capital (ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ; decision 20), as your settled *Spīritū Sānctō*; the draft had *sānctum* lower (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quandoquidem scriptum est: \\qt “Sancti estote: nam ego sum sanctus.”\\qt*
note: Lev 11:44 (19:2) after *scrīptum est:* in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB ("for it is written: “Be holy, because I am holy.”"); *Sānctī* capital as the quotation's first word, as 1573 (*ſcriptum eſt : Sancti eſtote*, canvas 920) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quod si Patrem invocatis eum, qui severissime ex cujusque facto judicat, vestrae peregrinationis tempus religiose transigite,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:16 closes the call to holiness with its text, and *Quod sī Patrem invocātis* opens the call to fear and the ransom (1:17–21); *Patrem* capital, God the Father whom they call on (εἰ πατέρα ἐπικαλεῖσθε; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Lustrate obediendo veritati vestros animos, per Spiritum ad fraternum amorem non fictum: et pura mente inter vos impense amate,
note: *per Spīritum* capital, the Holy Spirit (διὰ πνεύματος, the TR's reading, KJV "through the Spirit"; decision 20) (uncertain: the SBLGNT and the BSB lack the words, and 1573 prints *per ſpiritum*, lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Nam \\q1 \\qt “Mortales quidem omnes sunt herbae similes,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt omnisque hominis gloria est velut herbae flos.\\qt* \\q1 \\qt Aret herba, caditque flos:\\qt*
note: Isa 40:6–8 (1:24–25) as poetry in \\qt, three lines here and the fourth in 1:25, as the BSB sets it (*For, \\b \\q1 “All flesh is like grass …*); *Nam* (διότι) outside the marks with no colon added, as your Heb 10:37 *Etenim*; *Mortālēs* capital as the quotation's first word, as Heb 10:37 *Perpaulō*; Castellio renders *All flesh* as *mortālēs … omnēs* but it is the prophet's text (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: \\qt at Domini dictum manet in sempiternum.”\\qt* \\m Est autem hoc dictum illud, quod apud vos est nuntiatum.
note: Isa 40:8 closes the quotation (the BSB's q2 line), *at* lower case inside it (the draft's verse-opening capital came from stage 2's moved boundary); then Peter's comment as prose inside the verse (\\m), as the BSB and your 2 Cor 6:2 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Itaque sic in litteris habetur: \\q1 \\qt “Positurus sum in Sione lapidem angularem,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt lectum, eximium,\\qt* \\q1 \\qt cui qui confidet,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt non frustrabitur.”\\qt*
note: Isa 28:16 after *sīc in litterīs habētur:* (περιέχει ἐν γραφῇ) as poetry in \\qt, four lines as the BSB; *Positūrus* capital as the quotation's first word, as 1573 (*habetur : Poſiturus ſum*, canvas 920); the draft's comma after *eximium* left (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Vobis quidem fidentibus, eximius est: at diffidentibus, \\q1 \\qt “quem lapidem structores improbarunt,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt is ad anguli caput adhibitus est,”\\qt* \\q1 et \\qt “lapis, in quem impingant,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et petra, in quam illidant,”\\qt*
note: prose again after the poetry of 2:6 (`m`; the BSB's break not taken: *Vōbīs quidem fīdentibus, eximius est* applies the text just quoted); Ps 118:22 and Isa 8:14 as poetry in \\qt, two lines each as the BSB, each its own quotation; *quem* lower case, the quotation running on from *at diffīdentibus,* (Castellio builds it into his sentence); Peter's *et* (καί) between them at the head of the line, outside the marks, as Heb 10:37 *Etenim* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: qui in sermonem offendunt, ei inobedientes, ad quod erant destinati.
note: prose again after the poetry, as the BSB (*\\b \\m They stumble …*); *quī* lower case, the relative running on from 2:7 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: At vos lectum genus estis, regale sacerdotium, sancta gens, populus adquisitus, ut virtutes praedicetis ejus, qui vos ex tenebris in suam lucem admirabilem vocauit:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:8 closes the unbelievers' stumbling, and *At vōs lēctum genus estis* turns to the believers, a new sentence (2:9–10) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Carissimi, cohortor, ut inquilinos ac peregrinos: abstinete vos a corporeis cupiditatibus, quae contra animum militant.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Cārissimī, cohortor* opens the exhortations to conduct among the gentiles (2:11–12), a new address (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Servi, parete cum omni metu heris, non solum bonis et aequis, verum etiam iniquis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Servī, pārēte* turns to slaves, a new address, as *Similiter uxōrēs* (3:1) and *Virī itidem* (3:7); the BSB's breaks at 2:4, 2:16 left: *ad quem … accēdentēs* and *ut līberī* run on from the verse before (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Qui peccata nostra ipse suo corpore sustulit in patibulum, ut peccatis defuncti, justitiae vivamus: cujus vibice vos estis sanati.
note: *vīvāmus:* with 1573's colon (*iuſtitiæ viuamus : cuius / vibice*, canvas 921) for the draft's missing stop: *cujus vībīce …* is a new clause. 2:22–24 left as prose, unmarked, against the BSB's poetry and its quotation marks (Isa 53:9, 53:5): Castellio builds the prophet's words into three relative clauses on Christ (*Quī … Quī … Quī …*, *vōs estis sānātī* for the prophet's *we*), as he does 2:25 *quasi pālantēs ovēs* (uncertain) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: ut Sara obedivit Abrahamo, dominum eum appellans: cujus factae estis filiae, dum bene facitis, et nullo pavore terremini.
note: *dominum* lower case: Sarah's title for Abraham (κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα, BSB "calling him lord"), not God; 1573 *dominum eum appellans* (canvas 921) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Viri itidem habitate scienter cum uxoribus, muliebri vasi, ut infirmiori, tribuentes honorem, ut multiplicis beneficii et vitae coheredes, ne vestrae preces impediantur.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Virī itidem* turns from wives to husbands, a new address, as 3:1 *Similiter uxōrēs* opens one (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Nam \\q1 \\qt “Qui vitae cupidus est,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et felicia videre vult tempora,\\qt* \\q1 \\qt coërceat linguam suam a malitia,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et labra sua a loquendo fraudulenter:\\qt*
note: Ps 34:12–16 (3:10–12) as poetry in \\qt, as the BSB sets it (*For, \\b \\q1 “Whoever would love life …*), four lines here; *Nam* (γάρ) outside the marks, as 1:24; *Quī* capital as the quotation's first word (1573 *Nam qui vitæ*, lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: \\qt Declinet malum, et faciat bene:\\qt* \\q2 \\qt studeat paci, eamque persequatur.\\qt*
note: Ps 34:14 continued, two lines as the BSB; *Dēclīnet* keeps the draft's capital after 3:10's colon, as your settled letters do at a verse start after a colon (1573 runs it into its 10, lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: \\qt Habet enim Dominus oculos intentos in justos,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et aures ad eorum implorationem:\\qt* \\q1 \\qt faciem autem habet Dominus intentam\\qt* \\q2 \\qt in maleficos.”\\qt*
note: Ps 34:15–16 ended and the quotation closed, four lines as the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Ecquis vero est, qui vos laedat, si bonitatis imitatores sitis?
note: prose again after the poetry, so `m`; the BSB's break not taken: *Ecquis vērō est, quī vōs lædat* draws on the psalm's *faciem … in maleficōs*, and 3:14's paragraph follows (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quamquam etiam si propter justitiam feratis injuriam, felices estis. \\qt “Quae vero metuunt illi, vos ne metuite, neve turbamini,”\\qt*
note: Isa 8:12 in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB ("“Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”"); Castellio's *illī* and *vōs* fit it to the readers, but the words are the prophet's; closed before 3:15 *sed Dominum Deum … colite* (Isa 8:13, where the BSB's quotation also stops) (uncertain: an adapted citation without an introducing verb) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Siquidem Christus quoque semel pro nobis passus est, justus pro injustis, quo nos ad Deum adduceret, carne necatus, Spiritu in vitam revocatus:
note: *Spīritū* capital (ζῳοποιηθεὶς δὲ πνεύματι, BSB "made alive in the Spirit"), as your 1 Tim 3:16 *per Spīritum* in the same contrast with *carne* (uncertain: the KJV *by the Spirit*, but many read Christ's own spirit against his flesh; 1573 *ſpiritu*, lower; 4:6 *spīritū vīvant* left lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Omnium autem finis instat. Quocirca este frugi, et ad supplicationes sobrii,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Omnium autem fīnis īnstat* opens the closing exhortations of the section (4:7–11); the BSB's breaks at 4:4, 4:10, 4:14, 4:19 left, each running on (*Atque id*, *Prout quisque*, *Sī ob*, *Proinde*) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Si ob Christi nomen probris incessimini, felices estis, quod gloriosus divinusque Spiritus vos insidet. Per illos quidem vituperatur, sed per vos collaudatur.
note: *Spīritus* capital, the Spirit of glory and of God (τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα, BSB "the Spirit of glory and of God"; decision 20), the adjectives lower case as decision 20 sets them (uncertain: Castellio's adjectives *glōriōsus dīvīnusque* make it a description; 1573 *ſpiritus*, lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Et \\q1 \\qt “Si justus aegre servatur,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt impius et improbus ubi comparebit?”\\qt*
note: Prov 11:31 (LXX) as poetry in \\qt, two lines as the BSB (*And, \\b \\q1 “If it is hard …*); *Et* (καί) outside the marks, as 1:24 *Nam*; *Sī* capital as the quotation's first word; the question is the proverb's, so the question mark inside the marks (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Proinde qui Dei voluntate patiuntur adversa, ii recte faciendo conditori, ut fideli, suas commendent animas.
note: prose again after the poetry, so `m`; the BSB's break not taken as a paragraph: *Proinde* draws the conclusion of 4:12–18 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Similiter juniores parete senioribus, et omnes invicem obsequendo, modestia ornamini: nam \\q1 \\qt “Deus et superbis adversatur,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et modestorum fautor est.”\\qt*
note: Prov 3:34 (LXX) after *nam* as poetry in \\qt, two lines as the BSB and as your Jas 4:6 (the same words: *“Deus (inquit ille) et superbīs adversātur, et modestōrum fautor est.”*); *nam* outside the marks (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Quamobrem submittite vos potenti Dei manui, ut vos tempore curationis evehat,
note: prose again after the poetry, so `m`; the BSB's break not taken as a paragraph: *Quamobrem* draws the consequence of the proverb just quoted (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Sobrii este, vigilate: nam adversarius noster diabolus, ut leo rugiens circuit, quaerens, quem devoret.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Sōbriī este, vigilāte* opens the warning about the adversary (5:8–9), asyndetic after 5:7's comfort (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Per Sylvanum, vobis fidum, ut arbitror, fratrem, paucis scripsi, commonefaciens et testificans, istud esse verum Dei beneficium, in quo statis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Per Silvānum … paucīs scrīpsī* opens the letter's close and greetings (5:12–14), after the doxology of 5:11; the BSB's breaks at 5:13 and 5:14 left (one short closing paragraph) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: renati non ex mortali, sed immortali semine, per sermonem viventem Dei, et manentem in sempiternum.
note: *renātī* lower case: the sentence runs on from 1:22 *amāte,* (1573 *amate, 23 renati*, canvas 920), as the settled letters lower a verse start after a comma; the pipeline missed it because 1:22 has a layout line (Claude, 2026-11-12)
